shortDescription: Indian property developer Max Estates (BSE: 544008) NSE:MAXESTATES has put INR14.55mn ($156,004) into its subsidiary Acreage Builders Private Limited (ABPL) by taking up the subsidiary's entire issue of preference shares, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19, 2026.Max Estates…

children: has put INR14.55mn ($156,004) into its subsidiary Acreage Builders Private Limited (ABPL) by taking up the subsidiary's entire issue of preference shares, the company said in a stock exchange filing on November 19, 2026.

Max Estates acquired 1,455,166 redeemable preference shares carrying a 10% coupon, each with a face value of INR10, at par and for cash. The funds will raise ABPL's paid-up share capital to the level required by the Indian state of Haryana's Directorate of Town and Country Planning (DTCP).

ABPL is building Max District, a commercial real estate project in Sector 65 of Gurugram. Once the issue is complete, the subsidiary's paid-up capital will rise from INR5.45mn to INR20mn, according to the filing. The money will also support the unit's operations.

The shares are non-convertible, non-cumulative and non-participating. ABPL offered them as a rights issue to its existing shareholders. Max Estates took the full allotment after the other shareholders gave up their entitlements in its favour.
The transaction does not change the equity ownership of ABPL. Max Estates keeps a stake of roughly 51%, so ABPL remains its subsidiary.

The company classified the deal as a related party transaction because ABPL is a subsidiary. The filing said the subscription was made on an arm's-length basis and on the same terms offered to ABPL's other equity holders. The promoter group of Max Estates holds no direct stake in ABPL. Any interest it has comes only through its shareholding in the listed parent.
ABPL was incorporated in India on June 18, 2010. It has recorded no revenue from operations in the past three financial years, FY24 to FY26, because Max District is still under development.
The transaction needed no government or regulatory approvals. Max Estates has paid the full amount to ABPL and expects the acquisition to be completed by November 30, 2026.

title: India's Max Estates invests in subsidiary ABPL
